AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Studies often ignore time-varying confounding or use inappropriate methodology to adjust for time-varying confounding.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: We estimated the effect of ICU-acquired bacteraemia on ICU mortality and discharge using appropriate methodology.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting were used to estimate the ICU mortality and discharge associated with ICU-acquired bacteraemia among patients who stayed more than 2 days at the general ICU of a London teaching hospital and remained bacteraemia-free during those first two days. For comparison, the same associations were evaluated with 1) a conventional Cox model, adjusting for only baseline confounders and 2) a Cox model adjusting for baseline and time-varying confounders.

AbstractText.Label: FINDINGS
AbstractText.content: Using the marginal structural model with inverse probability weighting, bacteraemia was associated with an increase in ICU mortality (cause-specific hazard ratio [CSHR] 1.29, 95% CI 1.02-1.63) and a decrease in discharge (CSHR 0.52, 95% CI 0.45-0.60). By 60 days, among patients still in the ICU after 2 days and without prior bacteraemia, 8.0% of ICU-deaths could be prevented by preventing all ICU-acquired bacteraemia cases. The conventional Cox model adjusting for time-varying confounders gave substantially different results: CSHR 1.08 (95% CI 0.88-1.32) for ICU mortality and CSHR 0.68 (95% CI 0.60-0.77) for discharge.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: In our study, even after adjusting for the timing of acquiring bacteraemia and time-varying confounding using inverse probability weighting for marginal structural models, ICU-acquired bacteraemia was associated with a decreased daily ICU discharge risk and an increased risk of ICU mortality.
